sections.content: How many people are "animal care services occupations (other)"?

75,135 people

were counted on the census as "animal care services occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may care for animals held in kennels, stables, zoos and similar establishments, provide specialised training, grooming, clipping and trimming services for animals, search for and capture stray or nuisance dogs in public areas, and perform a variety of animal care tasks not elsewhere classified.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "animal care services occupations (other)" there were more women than men (80.4% compared with 19.6%).

This means "animal care services occupations (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 19.6% and women made up 80.4% of "animal care services occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "animal care services occupations (other)" included:

  • hairdressers and barbers
  • office managers
  • houseparents and residential wardens

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "animal care services occupations (other)", 14.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "animal care services occupations (other)" was 65 years or older.

We can look at who worked as "animal care services occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "animal care services occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "animal care services occupations (other)", 14.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (51.7% compared with 48.3%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (54.1%) than an employee (45.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Wiltshire, this is in the region of the South West.
